translations.answer: When the average production rate is below 250 Hz, the queue becomes full; if the full queue is interpreted as no target, zero value, or sudden retention, the joint targets are discontinuous. A more reliable approach is to resample at the target timestamp, interpolate within a bounded delay, and use last safe values, speed limits, or damping degradation for underload, while monitoring underrun.
translations.applicability: Applies to remote operation chains where the upper sampling rate is lower than the lower control rate.
translations.credibility.rationale: The rationale has not closed or there are unresolved conflicts; the source conclusions lack resolution; no reproducible record has been formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: Divide each 20 ms command into 5 parts for 4 ms execution.
translations.details.attempts.1: Discard 1/5 of the packets to reduce queue growth.
translations.details.attempts.2: Plan to switch the Python middle layer to C++.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Record the upper production timestamp, lower consumption timestamp, queue depth, packet loss count, and target continuity continuity.
translations.details.environments.0: Upper remote operation: 50 Hz/20 ms; lower C++ execution: 250 Hz/4 ms; ROS topic; maximum queue: 5000, cumulative queue after 10 packets: executed.
translations.details.limits.0: Raises questions about the factual basis of the article; no public timestamp curve, packet loss rate, or final rewrite result has been provided.
translations.details.outcomes.0: First scheme still causes queue overflow; second scheme reduces delay but causes underload jitter; final C++ rewrite direction is not publicly available or reproducible.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How can 50 Hz upper commands be stably sent to the 250 Hz lower execution loop?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why do queue overflow and queue underflow both manifest as robot jitter?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Limit joint speed, position increments, and torque before real machine testing; during queue anomalies, maintain last safe target or enter damping mode; do not directly convert missing frames into abrupt changes.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Inconsistent clock/scheduling between Python and C++.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Fixed five-part interpolation does not handle network jitter and production/consumption offset.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Discard new packets after queue overflow, leading to long delays and sudden large oscillations.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Delay reduces after discarding 1/5 packets, but the queue becomes full and continues to jitter.
translations.media_summaries.0: The Mermaid diagram in the text explains the structure of upper asynchronous write to the queue and lower strict periodic read from the queue; the diagram is conceptual and not real-time sequence evidence.
translations.source.locator: After discarding 1/5 packets, the queue is full and exhibits jitter.
translations.source.title: Queue Overflow and Underload Jitter in 50 Hz Remote Operation to 250 Hz Execution Layer
translations.title: Why does fixing some packets to reduce remote operation delay lead to continuous jitter?
